feedback: No race has run yet, so there is no earlier telemetry for this candidate or for any other. The bar for this iteration is that the candidate is valid and not obviously broken. I checked every field against the contract: all values are inside their limits, with 5 sensors matching 5 weights, a 0.012 m footprint, and last_direction line loss. Nothing is obviously broken, so I am approving it to race and get the first telemetry. Two things are untested and worth watching in the results. First, base_speed 1.8 may be too fast for the tightest bend, since the contract says 1.5 m/s average is needed to finish, and the first race will show whether the robot holds the line at that speed. Second, kp 1.5 with kd 0.05 gives a large differential (turn up to about 1050 PWM from a full-scale signal of 2), so oscillation on the slalom is plausible. Once the race reports, use these rules: if max_error approaches 0.06 or line_loss_events is above zero, lower base_speed or raise kp so the robot holds the line. If steering_oscillation is high while max_error is small, raise kd in small steps, since that damps the jitter without adding much noise. If completion is 0 with progress stalled, check the bend where it stopped before changing anything else. Keep ki at 0 unless rms_error shows a steady offset.
requested_changes: After the race, if max_error is near 0.06 or line_loss_events is above 0, reduce base_speed (for example 1.8 to 1.5) before changing kp, because the speed limit is the likelier cause on the first run.
If steering_oscillation is high while max_error stays small, raise kd from 0.05 to about 0.2 in one step and re-race; no earlier race supports a specific value yet.
If completion_time is above 3 s with completion 1, raise base_speed in small steps only if max_error and line_loss_events stay low; no earlier race has measured this trade-off yet.
